direct_answer:
Aker BP states that it conducted a double materiality assessment (DMA) in 2023 aligned with CSRD/ESRS and revised it in 2024 based on new information, implementation guidance and EFRAG’s draft oil & gas sector standard [Source 2]. The DMA maps impacts, risks and opportunities (IROs), their dependencies and their connection to Aker BP’s own operations and value chain [Source 2]. It considers activities, business relationships and geographies, focusing in own operations on oil and gas production (highest potential impact), in the upstream value chain mainly on development projects (construction activity), and it recognises downstream impacts related to the use of petroleum products [Source 2].

Methodologically, Aker BP describes a “systematic approach” covering both impact materiality (inside-out) and financial materiality (outside-in), explicitly including reputational risk and dependencies on natural, human and social resources within financial risks [Source 1]. It pays “special attention” to dependencies between impacts and related risks/opportunities [Source 1]. IROs are assessed and prioritised using severity × likelihood ratings (aligned with consequence × probability risk assessments) and company scales consistent with enterprise risk management; IROs are documented in the same tool as other company risks and prioritised/handled together [Source 1]. The DMA is described as a structured, iterative process: define business context (activities, business model, value chain, stakeholders, boundaries), identify actual/potential IROs using top-down and bottom-up approaches with internal/external stakeholder input and quantitative sources, assess/prioritise against impact and financial criteria using a standardised rating system, validate via management and Board, and monitor for updates [Source 12]. Governance oversight is described: all material IROs are reviewed by the Board of Directors (BoD), Audit & Risk Committee (ARC) and Executive Management Team (EMT) [Source 5].

Stakeholder engagement is incorporated into the DMA: Aker BP engages stakeholders through multiple channels (e.g., public consultations for PDO impact assessments, publishing impact assessments, whistleblowing channel) and includes stakeholder perspectives and priorities in the DMA [Source 3]. In 2024, this was achieved through interviews and workshops with internal management and subject matter experts; the process also builds on prior-year interviews involving owners, key suppliers, customers, NGOs and authorities [Source 3]. The ARC and EMT are kept informed about affected stakeholder views via channels including the DMA approval process and cases reported through the integrity channel [Source 1].

Sustainability matters identified as material from both an impact and a financial perspective (i.e., “strategic and highest priority” with high impact and high financial relevance) are: climate change, own workforce, pollution, business conduct, and resource use and circular economy [Source 3].
compliance_rationale: The passages provide a clear description of the DMA approach (double materiality, mapping IROs and dependencies, value chain focus, rating/prioritisation, integration with ERM, governance validation, and stakeholder engagement channels) and explicitly identify which topics are high on both impact and financial materiality (strategic/highest priority) [Source 1][Source 2][Source 3][Source 12][Source 5]. However, the retrieved evidence does not fully specify the qualitative/quantitative thresholds used to determine materiality beyond the general severity×likelihood approach, nor does it provide a complete list of all material matters that are simultaneously impact- and financially-material beyond the matrix caption’s summary.
disclosure_gaps: Explicit qualitative and/or quantitative thresholds (cut-offs) used to determine when an impact/risk/opportunity becomes material (beyond stating severity×likelihood ratings).
A complete, itemised list of sustainability matters that meet both impact and financial materiality criteria (the evidence only names the highest-priority set).

More detail on how interdependencies between impact and financial materiality are operationalised (e.g., how impact findings translate into financial risk/opportunity scoring) beyond stating that special attention is given to dependencies.
Evidence of direct engagement with affected stakeholders (as distinct from internal experts and prior-year stakeholder interviews) in the 2024 DMA process, including how their input changed outcomes.
Explicit description of how due diligence outcomes feed into the DMA outcomes (linkage is described at a high level, but not evidenced in the DMA passages provided).
key_findings: Aker BP conducted its first DMA in 2023 and revised it in 2024 using updated guidance and sector-specific draft standards [Source 2].
The DMA covers both impact (inside-out) and financial (outside-in) materiality, including reputational risk and dependencies on natural, human and social resources [Source 1].

IROs are mapped across own operations and the value chain, considering activities, business relationships and geographies; own-operations focus is oil and gas production, upstream focus is development projects, and downstream impacts relate to use of petroleum products [Source 2].
IROs are assessed/prioritised using severity×likelihood ratings aligned with enterprise risk management and documented/managed in the same tool as other company risks [Source 1].

Stakeholder perspectives are incorporated via multiple engagement channels; 2024 DMA used internal interviews/workshops and built on prior-year interviews with owners, suppliers, customers, NGOs and authorities [Source 3].

Topics identified as material from both impact and financial perspectives (strategic/highest priority) are: climate change, own workforce, pollution, business conduct, and resource use & circular economy [Source 3].
